theme: STRC hits $100 par and Saylor says 'We're back,' bitcoin holds near $80K, VanEck calls AI-pivot miners oversold after Riot's $28B lease, Musk floats space data centers as Texas AI builds face pushback, Microsoft flags DC delays, Meta sells AI bonds, neoclouds slide, and the S&P's post-midterm pattern is in focus.

items.title: Strategy's STRC preferred: weekly ATM estimate when it trades at or above par
items.picked: Strategy's STRC preferred hit its $100 par on Nov 4 for the first time since May, and Michael Saylor posted 'We're ₿ack,' a story trending on X and covered by CoinDesk. At or above par, Strategy can sell STRC again to fund bitcoin buys after months of buybacks.
items.matters: STRC is Strategy's main preferred funding line. How much volume trades above $100 decides whether it can raise cash for more bitcoin without selling common stock.
items.know: Mark's STRC ATM tab has $209.4M of total USD volume on Wed Nov 4, of which 19% ($38.9M) traded above $100. At the tab's 59% capture rate and 2.5% commission, that implies about $22.4M of ATM proceeds and about 279 bitcoin at the day's $80,207 average. Mon and Tue showed 0% above $100. The tab refreshes volume automatically; Thu and Fri are still blank.

items.title: Strategy capital raised by quarter: common, preferred, converts and bitcoin sold
items.picked: CEO Phong Le wrote on X that Strategy ranks fourth among US companies selling stock in 2026, behind SpaceX, Alphabet and Intel, calling it a 'Bitcoin capital cycle' as Strategy shares rose about 7% with bitcoin after the midterms, per TIKR.
items.matters: How Strategy funds its bitcoin pile — common equity, preferred or converts — sets the dilution and the fixed preferred dividend bill that preferred holders watch.
items.know: The tab has $7.4B raised in Q1 2026, $8.5B in Q2 and $5.8B in Q3, or about $21.7B year to date. Q3 was all common stock ($5.4B) plus $0.4B of bitcoin sold; preferred raised $0. Preferred raised $5.5B in Q2 at the peak. Q3 uses weekly 8-K ATM proceeds rather than the 10-Q cash-flow lines used for earlier quarters.

items.title: Bitcoin miners that pivoted to AI vs MARA and bitcoin
items.picked: VanEck said on Nov 5 that AI-pivot bitcoin miners look oversold after a 35% October drop, and Riot Platforms announced a $28B AI data-center lease that sent its shares up more than 14%, per CoinDesk and X news. IREN and CIFR still fell hard after the midterms on Texas data-center fears.
items.matters: The chart separates miners that leased power and space to AI from a pure miner like MARA, so you can see whether the AI pivot is being rewarded or punished.
items.know: Indexed to Dec 29 2023 = 100, the equal-weight IREN/CIFR/WULF basket was at 333.41 on Oct 30 2026, the tab's latest weekly close, down from a 601.89 peak on Sep 18. MARA was at 28.82 and bitcoin at 183.37 on the same day. The image and tab stop at Oct 30, so they miss this week's election-driven moves and Riot's lease news.

items.title: SpaceX capex by segment: Space, Starlink and AI
items.picked: Elon Musk posted that data centers in space are looking appealing after midterm results raised fresh hurdles for ground builds, a story trending on X. SpaceX has filed for up to a million solar-powered AI satellites, and Arthur Hayes warned of SpaceX share unlock dilution into 2027.
items.matters: Capex shows where SpaceX is actually putting money. AI spend now dwarfs Starlink and launch, which is why orbital compute talk lands as more than a meme.
items.know: On a trailing twelve months to Sep 2026, the tab has AI (xAI and X) capex of $44.65B, Starlink $5.47B and Space $4.85B. AI was $12.73B in 2025 and $5.63B in 2024. The image matches the TTM Sep '26 bar; ground data-center politics are the news hook, not a change in these book numbers.

items.title: Tesla vs the other Magnificent 7 and the Nasdaq-100 since end-2022
items.picked: Tesla fell about 5% after Democrats flipped Texas and Congress, per CoinDesk, while broader markets rallied. Tesla also joined other Mag 7 names objecting to third-party tokenized stock listings on an OKX-ICE venue, per X news.
items.matters: Tesla often moves with Mag 7 AI sentiment, but this chart shows whether it is keeping up with the other six and with the Nasdaq-100 on the same base.
items.know: Indexed to Dec 30 2022 = 100, Tesla was at 324.57 on Oct 30 2026, the tab's latest weekly close, against 499.59 for the equal-weight other Mag 7 and 259.47 for the Nasdaq-100. Tesla jumped from 287.97 on Oct 16 to 324.57 by Oct 30. The weekly series ends Oct 30, so it does not include this week's election drop.

items.title: Microsoft quarterly free cash flow: operating cash flow minus capex
items.picked: Microsoft cut its full-year capex outlook after third-party data-center delays from providers such as IREN, spending about $5B less than expected in the quarter, a story trending on X on Nov 5. IREN shares fell more than 11%.
items.matters: Free cash flow shows how much of Microsoft's cash generation is left after AI and cloud capex. When capex slips because of power and build delays, the AI timeline slips with it.
items.know: In the quarter to Jun 30 2026, the tab's latest point, Microsoft had $55.44B of operating cash flow and $35.80B of capex, for free cash flow of $19.64B, up from $15.80B in the March quarter. Capex has roughly doubled from $17.08B in the June 2025 quarter. The tab stops at Jun 2026, so it does not yet include the September quarter reported Oct 28.

items.title: Big Tech and CoreWeave debt balances used to fund AI builds
items.picked: Meta raised about $20–25B of dollar and euro bonds for AI data centers, drawing huge orders even after an S&P outlook cut, per X news. Hyperscaler and neocloud debt remains the core worry as Citrini and others warn AI infrastructure spending may be peaking.
items.matters: Debt is how much of the AI build is funded with borrowed money rather than free cash flow. Rising balances raise the cost of any slowdown in AI demand.
items.know: At the tab's latest point, labeled Jun 2026, Meta had $83.7B of debt, Amazon $133.0B, Alphabet $101.1B, Oracle $129.5B, Microsoft $40.3B and CoreWeave $35.6B. Meta was $58.7B in FY 2025 and $0 in FY 2021. This week's Meta bond sale is not in the tab yet.

items.title: Neocloud stocks in 2026: CRWV, NBIS, IREN, APLD, WULF and CIFR
items.picked: AI data-center names IREN and CIFR plunged after Democratic midterm wins and Texas data-center pushback, with IREN down more than 11% and CIFR nearly 20% in Wednesday's session per X news, even as the broad market rallied. Nebius has dropped about 40% in a month on Citrini's short call.
items.matters: Neoclouds are the purest listed bets on rented AI compute. This chart shows how far each has come or fallen in 2026 on the same base.
items.know: Indexed to Dec 31 2025 = 100, the tab's Oct 30 2026 close has NBIS at 184.1 (+84%), WULF at 102.1 (+2%), CRWV at 76.6 (−23%), APLD at 72.7 (−27%), IREN at 63.4 (−37%) and CIFR at 49.4 (−51%). The series was refreshed Nov 2 and ends Oct 30, so it misses this week's election session.

items.title: S&P 500 path in midterm years vs the average of all years
items.picked: A story trending on X notes the S&P 500 has risen in the 12 months after every midterm since 1942, averaging about 13%, and Democrats' sweep set up divided government with President Trump. SPY jumped about 1.65% to $766.81 on Nov 4 as markets cheered the results.
items.matters: Midterm years are often weak into the vote and stronger after. Putting 2026 on the same calendar as past midterms shows whether this cycle is following that script.
items.know: Indexed to the prior year-end = 100, 2026 was at 110.73 on trading day 209, the tab's latest 2026 point, against 97.99 for the average midterm year (1974–2022) and 105.81 for the average of all years (1971–2025) on that day. So 2026 is still well ahead of the typical midterm path. The 2026 series stops at day 209 (late October) and does not include this week's post-election rally.
